clips.title: Enabling PR and ephemeral environments at enterprise scale
clips.why: The problem this lesson starts from, in a real team's words: one shared test environment, everybody waiting for it, and the case for one environment per pull request.
look: What goes wrong when many teams share one staging or QA environment.
Why an environment that exists only for one pull request removes the waiting.
What it costs, and why such environments must be thrown away afterwards.
clips.after: fcp's QA lock is this shared environment, and FCP Lab per run is the environment per pull request.

clips.title: Kubernetes Ephemeral (Temporary) Environments Explained
clips.why: Viktor Farcic explains preview or pull request environments: a full copy of the system, created for one change and deleted with it.
look: A preview environment is created when the pull request opens and removed when it closes.
It runs the real application, so the tests check the real thing, not a stand-in.
Why each pull request needs its own name and its own data.
clips.after: Our version is even shorter-lived: one Lab per CI run, named ci-<run id>, gone when the job ends.

clips.title: GitHub Actions Concurrency Explained | Prevent Overlapping Workflow Runs
clips.why: How a concurrency group with the branch in its name works, which is exactly the smoke workflow's group.
look: A fixed group name makes every run in the repo wait for the same lock.
Putting github.ref into the name gives each branch its own group.
cancel-in-progress decides whether a newer run waits or stops the older one.
clips.after: QA uses a fixed name and waits; the Lab smoke uses lab-smoke-<workflow>-<branch> and cancels the outdated run.

practice.q: Which concurrency setting fits the Lab smoke workflow, where every run boots its own Lab?

options.why: A fixed name puts every pull request in one queue, which brings back the wait the Lab was meant to remove.

options.text: group: lab-smoke-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true
options.why: Each branch has its own group, so pull requests never wait for each other, and a newer push stops the outdated run of the same branch.
Every run gets its own group, so nothing ever cancels an outdated run of the same branch. It does no harm, but it wastes Lab time.

practice.q: Finish the command so this run gets a private stack whose containers, network and data belong to it alone.
practice.hint: The flag that sets the compose project name.
practice.why: The project name prefixes every container, network and volume, so two projects never share anything.

practice.q: Put one Lab smoke run for a pull request in order.
items: The images job finds the commit's tag in the registry, or builds and pushes it once
The smoke job boots a Lab named ci-<run id> from those images
The core proof, a few Playwright specs and the contract suites run
Something failed, so lab compare boots main's Lab and sorts each failure
The reports are uploaded and the Lab is thrown away with the runner
practice.why: Build once, boot privately, test, compare only when needed, and leave nothing behind for the next run.

practice.q: Why does the images job use concurrency: lab-images-${{ github.sha }} without cancel-in-progress?

options.text: So the second caller of a commit waits, then finds the tag and skips the build.
options.why: Without the group, two callers starting at once both see no tag and both build. Cancelling would throw away a build someone needs.

options.text: So only one commit in the repo can build at a time.
options.why: The commit is in the name, so different commits build at the same time.

options.text: So a newer commit stops the older commit's build.
options.why: That would need cancel-in-progress and a branch name in the group. Here every commit keeps its own build.

practice.q: The smoke run is red. lab compare says main fails the same test the same way. What does that tell the pull request's author?

options.text: The pull request broke the test and must fix it.
options.why: If main fails the same way, the failure was there before this change.

options.text: The test is already failing on main, so this change did not cause it.
options.why: That is the "already failing on main" verdict. Someone should fix main, but this pull request is not the cause.

options.text: The Lab is broken and the result means nothing.
options.why: The Lab booted and ran on both sides. The comparison is the useful part.
